findings.title: Global group view permission grants group management
findings.body: `canManage()` evaluates both the `view` and `manage` scopes on the all-groups resource. This method guards write operations such as `POST /groups`, so an administrator granted only the read-only all-groups `view` scope can create groups (and receive other operations guarded by global `requireManage`). Only the `manage` scope should satisfy this check.

findings.title: Group member visibility collects authorization resource IDs instead of group IDs
findings.body: While iterating group authorization resources, this passes `groupResource.getId()` to `hasPermission` and adds that same value to `granted`. `getId()` is the authorization Resource's ID, whereas per-group resources are named with the Keycloak group ID and `UserModel.GROUPS` is consumed as a set of Keycloak group IDs. Consequently, per-group `view-members`/`manage-members` permissions are not found here and the user search filter receives unusable IDs, so administrators cannot discover members through user search based on a specific group permission. Use `groupResource.getName()` (the group ID) for both the permission lookup and returned set.

findings.title: Existing admin-permissions clients are never upgraded with Groups resources and scopes
findings.body: `init` returns as soon as an admin-permissions client already exists. After this schema adds the Groups resource type and its three new scopes, realms that enabled V2 before this release retain a resource server without those scopes or the all-groups resource. Creating a Groups scope permission will fail scope validation, and group permission evaluation can fall through with a null all-groups resource. Initialization needs an upgrade/reconciliation path that adds missing schema scopes and type resources to existing admin-permissions clients.
